title: Service Discovery in Spring Boot Microservices

cards.title: The Dynamic IP Problem in Microservices
cards.content:
In traditional monolithic applications, components communicate in-process or via static backend URLs. However, modern microservice architectures deployed on auto-scaling cloud environments face a dynamic network location problem.

Key challenges include:

  • Dynamic Auto-scaling: Instances scale up or down dynamically based on traffic.
  • Ephemeral Containers: IP addresses change constantly whenever pods or containers restart.
  • Manual Management Complexity: Hardcoding IP addresses or maintaining dynamic DNS records manually is fragile and unsustainable.

cards.title: What is Service Discovery?
cards.content:
Service Discovery acts as a dynamic lookup registry (like a phonebook) for microservices.

Instead of hardcoding hostnames and ports, services interact via a central Service Registry:

  1. Registration: Microservice instances register their host, port, and health status upon startup.
  2. Discovery: Client services query the registry to locate available instances of target services.
  3. Deregistration: Instances unregister on graceful shutdown or are evicted when unhealthy.

cards.title: Client-Side vs. Server-Side Discovery
cards.content:
There are two main architectural patterns for Service Discovery:

1. Client-Side Discovery

The client queries the service registry directly, receives a list of available instances, and selects one using a client-side load balancing algorithm (e.g., Spring Cloud Eureka + Spring Cloud LoadBalancer).

2. Server-Side Discovery

The client makes a request to a router/load balancer (e.g., AWS ALB or Kubernetes Service). The load balancer queries the registry and routes the request (e.g., Kubernetes DNS & ClusterIP).

cards.title: Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka Overview
cards.content:
Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka is one of the most widely used Service Discovery toolsets in the Java ecosystem.

  • Eureka Server: The central service registry server application where all services register.
  • Eureka Client: A Java/Spring Boot application that registers itself with Eureka Server and queries it to locate other services.
// Dependency in pom.xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.cloud</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-cloud-starter-netflix-eureka-server</artifactId>
</dependency>

content.text: To turn a Spring Boot application into a Eureka Service Registry server, annotate the main class with @___EurekaServer.

cards.title: Configuring Eureka Server
cards.content:
When running a standalone Eureka Server, it shouldn't try to register with itself as a client.

Example application.yml:

server:
  port: 8761

eureka:
  client:
    register-with-eureka: false
    fetch-registry: false
  server:
    enable-self-preservation: true

cards.title: Heartbeats & Self-Preservation Mode
cards.content:
Eureka clients send periodic heartbeats (default every 30 seconds) to inform the server that they are alive.

Self-Preservation Mode

If network issues occur, Eureka Server might stop receiving heartbeats from many instances simultaneously. Instead of evicting all instances from the registry, Eureka enters Self-Preservation Mode:

  • It freezes registry evictions to protect against transient network partitions.
  • It serves stale client instance data until network stability is restored.

cards.title: Client-Side Call with Spring Cloud LoadBalancer
cards.content:
Once Eureka Client resolves hostnames, Spring Cloud LoadBalancer enables inter-service HTTP calls using virtual service names instead of physical IPs.

@Bean
@LoadBalanced
public RestTemplate restTemplate() {
    return new RestTemplate();
}

// Usage inside service layer:
String response = restTemplate.getForObject("http://ORDER-SERVICE/orders/1", String.class);

cards.title: Alternative Discovery Tools: Consul & Kubernetes
cards.content:
While Netflix Eureka is standard in Spring Cloud, alternative solutions exist for diverse enterprise stacks:

  • HashiCorp Consul: Language-agnostic service discovery providing key-value store, health checks, and service mesh support. Integrated via spring-cloud-starter-consul-discovery.
  • Kubernetes Native Discovery: Utilizes Kubernetes native DNS and Services (`Kube-DNS` / `CoreDNS`), avoiding the need for a dedicated Spring Cloud Eureka Server cluster.
